requirements.evidence: Most task pieces are attempted: enum (app/Enums/QueuePermission.php:5-7), model (app/Models/QueueAccess.php:15-27), factory (database/factories/QueueAccessFactory.php:12-26), three actions, policy, and both call paths authorized (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:33, app/Models/Ticket.php:99). But core requirements fail: no migration for the queue_access table is present anywhere in change.diff; the model has no `$table` override so Eloquent targets `queue_accesses` (app/Models/QueueAccess.php:11-17); `QueuePolicy::create` has an unresolvable type hint (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:16); Ticket::call authorizes after the LogicException (app/Models/Ticket.php:95-99); UpdateQueue has no duplicate-race handling (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:29-47); and the three doc updates (business-rules, database-schema, CHANGELOG) are absent.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes correctly live in app/Actions/* with authorization inside, `$fillable` is set deliberately (app/Models/QueueAccess.php:15), and the enum/model/factory contract is followed. Deviations: no tests at all despite the TDD convention; no generated migration with a reversible down() for queue_access; required docs not kept in sync (docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md, CHANGELOG.md absent from the diff); a duplicate, unregistered AuthServiceProvider (app/Providers/AuthServiceProvider.php:1-22); imports not Pint-sorted (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:6-9).

security.evidence: Authorization is present on create/update/manageAccess/call and validation is server-side (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:18-58, app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:25-41), and the `call` policy correctly denies corrupted non-array permissions (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:53-58). Gaps: authorization uses the ambient Auth user via `Gate::authorize` instead of the passed actor (app/Models/Ticket.php:99, app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:24, app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:33), contradicting the contract's `Gate::forUser($user)`; SetQueueAccess performs the cross-entity check before authorizing, so non-managers receive a ValidationException rather than AuthorizationException and can probe entity membership (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:18-24). No exploitable unauthorized write was found.

tests.evidence: change.diff contains no test files at all; there are no Pest/PHPUnit tests for CreateQueue, UpdateQueue, SetQueueAccess, QueuePolicy or the new call authorization, so no happy-path, validation, unauthorized-call or corrupted-permissions coverage exists.

simplicity.evidence: The actions are small and direct and reuse Gate/ValidationException/updateOrCreate, but there is avoidable duplication and dead code: policies are registered twice (app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:35-36 and the unused app/Providers/AuthServiceProvider.php:14-17), `if (!is_array($permissions))` is dead because the parameter is typed array (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:27), unused imports remain (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:8-9, app/Models/QueueAccess.php:6), and the factory creates rows inside definition() (database/factories/QueueAccessFactory.php:18-19).

readability.evidence: Names are clear and methods are short, but style is loose: unused imports (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:8-9, app/Models/QueueAccess.php:6), a redundant inline comment restating the type (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:18), import ordering that would fail Pint (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:6-9), and a speculative `'labels_i18n' => null` (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:37) make it understandable but not clean.

scope.evidence: Nearly every file maps directly to the task (three actions, enum, model, factory, policy, call-path edits), but the change adds an unasked-for second service provider (app/Providers/AuthServiceProvider.php:1-22) plus duplicate policy registration (app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:35-36), which is unrelated to the requested slice.

issues.explanation: The required queue_access table is never created: no migration ships with the change, so SetQueueAccess, the policy and the factory all query a non-existent table.
The model does not set `protected $table = 'queue_access'`, so Eloquent derives `queue_accesses` instead of the contract's `queue_access` table, breaking every query even once a migration exists.
The `create` type hint `App\Models\Entity` inside namespace App\Policies resolves to `App\Policies\App\Models\Entity`, so an Entity argument never matches and queue creation always fails.
Authorization is placed after the "Only waiting tickets" LogicException, but the task requires the AuthorizationException first, including when the ticket was already called.
No Pest/PHPUnit tests accompany any of the new actions, policy, model or call-path authorization, violating the project's test-first convention and leaving every requirement unverified.
The task explicitly requires updating these three documents, and the change updates none of them, so the docs are now stale.

Authorizing with `Gate::authorize` checks the ambient authenticated user rather than the `$user`/`$actor` passed to the action; `Ticket::call(User $user)` can therefore evaluate permissions for the wrong principal, whereas the contract requires `Gate::forUser($user)`.
The cross-entity check runs before `Gate::authorize`, so a non-manager gets a ValidationException instead of an AuthorizationException and can probe whether a membership and queue share an entity.
Slug updates lack the QueryException-to-ValidationException handling used in CreateQueue, so losing a uniqueness race on update surfaces a raw QueryException instead of a ValidationException.

This new provider duplicates the Gate::policy registrations already made in AppServiceProvider and is not registered in bootstrap/providers.php (no such change), so it is dead code; the policy is auto-discovered anyway.
Lowercasing each permission accepts values such as `CALL`, which are not one of the known permission strings the task says must be rejected.
The `!is_array($permissions)` guard is dead code because the parameter is already type-hinted `array`.
`definition()` creates a Queue and an EntityMembership as a side effect, so extra rows are persisted even when callers override those attributes.
Unused imports (`UserRole`, `EntityMembership`, `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\Fillable`) add noise and would be removed by tooling.
An explicitly empty slug falls back to the name-derived slug instead of being validated, which silently ignores the caller's input.
`isUniqueViolation` treats any SQLSTATE 23000 (also foreign-key/NOT NULL violations) as a duplicate slug and then sniffs message text, which can misreport unrelated integrity errors.

review.summary: The change adds the CreateQueue/UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess actions, QueueAccess model and factory, QueuePermission enum, QueuePolicy, and call authorization in both call paths. It cannot work as delivered: the queue_access migration is missing, the model targets the wrong table, the create policy has an unresolvable type hint, Ticket::call authorizes in the wrong order, and there are no tests or doc updates. Multiple blockers mean the pull request needs substantial rework before merge.
